claims.text: A roughly 100 nm CrN interlayer can be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The CrN interlayer will be adherent to both the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The CrN interlayer will remain stable and ceramic-like under the proposed exposure conditions.
CrN minimizes mutual solubility and interdiffusion between Cr and the zirconium alloy at elevated temperature.
The CrN interlayer physically restricts atomic diffusion of chromium into zirconium at high temperature.
CrN remains chemically inert during transient high-temperature steam exposure.
Restricting Cr–Zr interdiffusion prevents formation of brittle interfacial phases.
Brittle phases produced by Cr–Zr interdiffusion lead to coating degradation.
Elemental Cr-coated zirconium-alloy cladding without an interlayer is prone to accelerated degradation caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion in high-temperature steam.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated control, the CrN-interlayered system will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature exposure.
Reduced interdiffusion will preserve a distinct interface between the Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
Preserving the distinct interface will prolong coating effectiveness and adhesion.
The CrN-interlayered coating will preserve protection during prolonged subcritical-water exposure near 320°C and below approximately 350°C.
The CrN-interlayered coating will preserve protection during steam exposure at approximately 1200°C for about 5 seconds.
